headline_marked: Police tighten security after [[BRAC University receives bomb threat]] via email
headline: Police tighten security after BRAC University receives bomb threat via email
summary: Authorities are on high alert after an anonymous email threatened mass bombings at the campus on Tuesday.
details: BRAC University authorities received a threatening email on Sunday evening around 6:45 PM. The message, sent from an address listed as '[email protected]', threatened multiple bomb attacks on the campus for Tuesday.
The email warned that 'none of you can stop what is about to happen,' creating immediate concern for the safety of students and staff.
In response, the university administration filed a General Diary (GD) with the Badda Police Station to report the threat.
Badda Police Station OC Kazi Md. Nasirul Amin confirmed that security has been significantly tightened across the campus in the Merul Badda area.
Police are currently investigating the matter to identify the sender of the email and determine the validity of the threat.
The university remains on high alert as authorities work to track down the perpetrator.

headline_marked: 9 deaths in 24 hours: [[Dengue death toll rises to 271]] this year
headline: 9 deaths in 24 hours: Dengue death toll rises to 271 this year
summary: Another 1,902 patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in a single day, according to the DGHS.
details: Bangladesh has reported nine more dengue deaths in a 24-hour period, bringing the total yearly death toll to 271, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
In the last 24 hours, 1,902 new patients were admitted to hospitals nationwide. This includes 206 in Dhaka North City Corporation and 223 in Dhaka South.
Other significant admissions occurred in Khulna (306), Chattogram (272), and Barishal (216), while Mymensingh, Rajshahi, Rangpur, and Sylhet also reported cases.
A total of 88,360 people have been hospitalised with dengue this year, with 82,335 patients already discharged.
September was the most severe month this year, recording 43,774 admissions and 148 deaths.
The health directorate has tracked these figures since 2000. In 2023, the country saw its highest annual figures with 321,179 admissions and 1,705 deaths.
caption:
9 deaths in just 24 hours. The dengue crisis continues to climb.

Bangladesh has reported nine more dengue deaths in a 24-hour period, bringing the total yearly death toll to 271, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

In the last 24 hours, 1,902 new patients were admitted to hospitals nationwide. This includes 206 in Dhaka North City Corporation and 223 in Dhaka South.

Other significant admissions occurred in Khulna (306), Chattogram (272), and Barishal (216), while Mymensingh, Rajshahi, Rangpur, and Sylhet also reported cases.

A total of 88,360 people have been hospitalised with dengue this year, with 82,335 patients already discharged.

September was the most severe month this year, recording 43,774 admissions and 148 deaths.

The health directorate has tracked these figures since 2000. In 2023, the country saw its highest annual figures with 321,179 admissions and 1,705 deaths.
